title: Converge Embed+Rank API contracts: error mapping, cursor contract, and SDK shim
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: Multiple client SDKs and downstream customers rely on slightly different semantics between the embeddings endpoint and the rerank endpoint (error codes, retry hints, and cursor semantics). This causes broken SDK behavior and inconsistent UX when customers upgrade the platform or switch between hosted/dedicated/private modes. Goal: converge the two endpoints to a single, well-documented HTTP contract without breaking existing clients during a 3-month migration window. Scope: HTTP status mapping, Retry-After semantics, error bodies (code/typology), limit/offset vs opaque cursor support, SDK shim behavior for older clients, and telemetry hooks for measuring migration progress.
acceptance_criteria: Define canonical HTTP status mappings for all common failure classes and publish in the API spec
Implement opaque cursor format + stable query params (limit, cursor) and ensure bidirectional compatibility with legacy page-based queries
SDK shim releases for Node/Python/Go translate legacy pagination -> new cursor and surface consistent retry fields
Integration tests cover 429, 4xx client errors (400/422), 5xx server errors and partial results semantics for both embeddings and rerank endpoints
Docs and migration guide published with code samples and recommended backoff strategies
notes: Decision log 2025-02-09: prefer 400 for malformed requests, 422 for semantic validation failures (e.g., embedding vector length mismatch), 429 for rate limits with Retry-After in seconds, 503 for temporary capacity fallbacks with Retry-After optional.
Trade-off: keeping a visible Retry-After header increases response size but improves client retry behavior; chosen to include Retry-After for 429 and 503 where helpful.
Fallback plan: rerank will fall back to a cheaper approximate scorer when capacity constrained; the response must include a 'fallback_variant' field in the structured error body.

Cursor format: base64-encoded JSON blob containing (cursor_id, seq, server_region) to allow server-driven evolution. The API will accept numeric page and offset parameters for 6 months and emit deprecation warnings in response headers.

SDK shim approach: translate legacy ?page=..&per_page=.. into a temporary cursor via a server-side mapping table for 90 days to avoid client changes during initial rollout. After 90 days, mapping becomes read-only and will be removed after 180 days (announcement cycle).
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for mapping logic in runtime; 2) Contract tests exercising every error class for embeddings and rerank; 3) E2E using Node and Python SDKs verifying shim translation; 4) Load tests to ensure header injection (deprecation) does not regress latency.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (week 0-2): spec published + SDK shims released; Phase 2 (week 3-6): enable cursor acceptance and emit deprecation headers for legacy query params; Phase 3 (week 7-12): telemetry gating (95% of traffic using new cursors) then schedule removal of server-side legacy mapping; Phase 4: final deprecation removal announced and executed at 180 days.
open_questions: Do enterprise private deployments get the server-side mapping table applied automatically or behind an opt-in flag?
Should we add a machine-readable error code namespace (e.g., x-error-code) in addition to HTTP status for easier SDK handling?
How to signal partial results for rerank when one shard times out: use 206 + structured body or 200 with 'partial':true?
